contraindications: Migraine with brainstem aura and hemiplegic migraine: triptans are excluded by the product labels because of a theoretical vasoconstrictive risk and no trial data; avoid.
Ergot derivatives: avoid in migraine with brainstem aura for the same reason.
Triptans are also contraindicated by label after stroke or TIA, in ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease and uncontrolled hypertension.
interactions: Rigevidon (ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel) and ibuprofen (current): no clinically relevant interaction with triptans.
output.summary: Triptans and ergots are label-restricted in migraine with brainstem aura; an NSAID with an antiemetic is the usual acute treatment.
warnings: AHS 2021 notes emerging observational data that triptans may be safe in migraine with brainstem aura, but the label restriction stands; any use is a specialist decision.
Do not take a triptan within 24 hours of an ergot derivative.

contraindications: Propranolol: asthma, second- or third-degree heart block, marked bradycardia.

Topiramate with ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel or a progestogen-only pill: enzyme induction reduces contraceptive efficacy at 200 mg a day or more.
Amitriptyline, propranolol and candesartan: no interaction with levonorgestrel or desogestrel.
output.proposed: Migraine preventive options: propranolol, amitriptyline, topiramate, candesartan
output.summary: Propranolol, amitriptyline, candesartan and topiramate each have patient-level cautions; topiramate and valproate carry pregnancy restrictions.
warnings: Propranolol may worsen depression and fatigue and reduce exercise tolerance.
Amitriptyline: sedation, dry mouth, weight gain; caution in arrhythmia.
Topiramate is teratogenic: use only under a pregnancy prevention programme with highly effective contraception (MHRA 2024).
Sodium valproate: not for women who can become pregnant unless a pregnancy prevention programme applies.

results.finding: Attacks meet the criteria for migraine with aura and include at least two fully reversible brainstem symptoms (dysarthria, vertigo, tinnitus, hypacusis, diplopia, ataxia not attributable to sensory deficit, decreased level of consciousness), with no motor or retinal symptoms. Typical aura symptoms accompany the brainstem symptoms in most attacks; the older term basilar-type migraine was dropped because basilar artery involvement is unlikely.
results.source: Headache Classification Committee of the IHS. ICHD-3. Cephalalgia 2018;38:1-211 (1.2.2 Migraine with brainstem aura)

output.summary: Brainstem aura is defined by at least two reversible brainstem symptoms within an otherwise typical migraine aura, without motor or retinal symptoms.

action_criteria.rationale: The diagnosis of brainstem aura is clinical; the history must count the brainstem symptoms, exclude motor and retinal symptoms and apply the 3-of-6 rule, which here is met only through duration, the positive symptom and the headache.

action_criteria.rationale: Brainstem aura of recent onset is a red flag; MRI excludes a posterior fossa lesion or infarct and is preferred to CT (Evans RW et al., Headache 2020;60:318-336; AAN 2000).

action_criteria.label: Search the literature on migraine with brainstem aura

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe triptans or ergot derivatives: they are avoided in migraine with brainstem aura; use an NSAID with an antiemetic.
Do not continue or start combined hormonal contraception (pill, patch or ring): migraine with aura is UKMEC category 4; offer a progestogen-only method or an IUD.
Do not offer sodium valproate for prevention: she can become pregnant and valproate is restricted to use under a pregnancy prevention programme when nothing else works (MHRA).
required_recommendations: Stop Rigevidon now: combined hormonal contraception is UKMEC category 4 in migraine with aura; switch without a gap to a progestogen-only pill (desogestrel 75 micrograms), implant, levonorgestrel IUS or copper IUD.

Explain that bilateral visual aura with vertigo, unsteadiness and slurred speech followed by headache is migraine with brainstem aura, not basilar insufficiency or a tumour, and that the MRI is normal.

For acute attacks use an NSAID at an adequate dose (naproxen 500 mg or ibuprofen 600 mg) with an antiemetic (metoclopramide 10 mg or prochlorperazine) at headache onset; avoid triptans and ergots in migraine with brainstem aura.

Offer migraine prevention because the brainstem aura recurs (AHS 2021): amitriptyline 10 mg at night titrated to 25-50 mg, or propranolol 40 mg twice daily titrated to 80-160 mg a day if she has no asthma or depression; review at 8-12 weeks with a headache diary.

If topiramate is chosen, start it only with highly effective contraception (copper or hormonal IUD, or implant) under the topiramate pregnancy prevention programme; it reduces the efficacy of oral and progestogen-only pills.

avoided_actions.rationale: Head CT is less sensitive than MRI for migraine-relevant structural causes and is not indicated in typical migraine with aura; even when imaging is warranted, MRI is preferred
Lumbar puncture is not indicated in migraine with aura; reserve for suspected SAH (with normal CT) or meningitis; neither is present here
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated in typical migraine with aura; no role unless cardioembolic stroke is on the differential
EEG is not indicated for migraine with aura; reserve for cases where focal seizure is genuinely on the differential

accepted: Migraine with brainstem aura (ICHD-3 1.2.2); combined OCP contraindicated (WHO Category 4); preventive therapy indicated

differential.key_features: Three stereotyped attacks over 4 months with positive visual phenomena, brainstem symptoms lasting 15-20 minutes and a following migrainous headache, in a 33-year-old without vascular risk factors; normal interictal examination and MRI.

Vertigo is part of her attacks, but each attack also has visual aura, dysarthria and ataxia that meet ICHD-3 1.2.2, which takes precedence (vestibular migraine, appendix A1.6.6, applies when no other ICHD-3 diagnosis fits).
Episodic, fully reversible symptoms with a normal interictal examination; MRI shows a normal brainstem, cerebellum and craniocervical junction.
No neck pain or trauma, three stereotyped self-limited attacks over 4 months and no fixed deficit; no infarct on MRI.

key_clinical_evidence: Three attacks of bilateral visual aura with vertigo, ataxia and dysarthria lasting 15-20 minutes, followed by an occipital migrainous headache: ICHD-3 1.2.2 (3 of 6 C characteristics, three brainstem symptoms, no motor or retinal symptoms).
Bilateral visual aura is compatible with migraine aura; the absence of a unilateral symptom does not exclude it when three other C characteristics are present.
She takes Rigevidon: combined hormonal contraception is UKMEC category 4 with migraine aura and must be stopped.
Triptans and ergots are label-restricted in brainstem aura; recurrent brainstem aura is an indication to consider prevention (AHS 2021).
MRI shows a normal posterior fossa and only two non-specific punctate white matter hyperintensities.

findings.result: Three stereotyped attacks in 4 months; none before.

Visual: flashing coloured lights and zigzag patterns in both visual fields at once. Brainstem: rotatory vertigo, unsteadiness walking a straight line (no limb weakness or numbness), slurred articulation. No weakness, no monocular visual loss. Fully reversible.
No gradual spread described; the visual disturbance involves both fields from the start.
Vertigo, unsteadiness and slurred speech accompany the visual aura rather than follow it.
No unilateral symptom: visual aura bilateral; dysarthria and vertigo are not lateralised.
Bilateral occipital pulsating headache, 8/10, after the aura resolves, with nausea, vomiting and photophobia, lasting 6-10 hours.
Three brainstem symptoms (dysarthria, vertigo, ataxia not attributable to sensory deficit); no motor or retinal symptoms.

Headache-free. Visual fields full, no nystagmus, pursuit, saccades and vestibulo-ocular reflex normal, power 5/5, sensation intact, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, plantars flexor, finger-nose and heel-shin normal, gait normal without truncal ataxia. BP 116/70 mmHg.

Brainstem aura and recent onset of a new headache type (4 months): present. Systemic symptoms, history of neoplasm, persisting deficit, thunderclap onset, age over 50, positional or Valsalva trigger, papilloedema, progressive headache, pregnancy or puerperium, painful eye, head trauma, immune suppression and analgesic overuse: absent.

Combined oral contraceptive (ethinylestradiol 30 micrograms with levonorgestrel 150 micrograms); ibuprofen 400 mg as needed with partial relief. Non-smoker, no hypertension. Mother has migraine without aura.

Ventricles and sulci normal for age.

patient.history_present_illness:
A 33-year-old Japanese-Australian woman presented to the neurology outpatient clinic with three episodes over the past 4 months that she describes as extremely alarming. Each episode begins with flashing, coloured lights and undulating zigzag patterns in both visual fields simultaneously — unlike descriptions she has read of typical migraine aura, which she believes only affects one eye. The visual phenomenon is accompanied by a sensation of the world spinning or 'rocking like a boat' (vertigo), difficulty walking a straight line, and slurred speech lasting approximately 15-20 minutes. She feels extremely nauseated during the episode. After these symptoms resolve, she develops a severe bilateral occipital headache (8/10) pulsating in quality with nausea and photophobia, lasting 6-10 hours. She vomits during the headache phase.

She is alarmed that the visual phenomenon is bilateral, that she has vertigo and ataxia, and that her speech is affected — features she read online suggest 'basilar artery insufficiency' or a brain tumour rather than simple migraine. She has seen two general practitioners who were also uncertain and ordered brain imaging urgently. She has been very anxious about these episodes and has been researching online extensively. Her mother had migraines without aura. She is on the combined oral contraceptive pill (Rigevidon — EE 30 mcg + levonorgestrel). She is a software engineer, non-smoker, no alcohol.
